text:
Alex: Heads-up — DCGM exporter started failing on ~8 nodes in eu-west-1 after the kernel patch last night. Seeing `modprobe nvidia` errors and the exporter OOMing in the logs. Anyone on call?
Priya: I saw alerts from Prometheus about `dcgm_up == 0` and node_exporter spikes. Can you paste the logs?
Alex: Paste below — short snippet from the node: ```May 3 03:12:11 gpu-node-42 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
May 3 03:12:12 dcgm-exporter[2145]: panic: failed to init GPU probe: nvmlInit failed: unknown error
May 3 03:12:12 systemd[1]: dcgm-exporter.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=2/INVALIDARG```
Sam: Hmm kernel signature check kicked in after the vendor kernel update. The module can't load so `nvidia-smi` returns no devices. DCGM depends on nvml.
Priya: Are these the new burst instances we rolled yesterday? I remember a slightly different OS image for g4dn-family in eu-west-1.
Alex: Yes — rolling patch + image bump. Looks like the kernel on those nodes enforces signed modules. Our NVIDIA module wasn't built/signed in the image.
infra-bot: [alert] prometheus/alertmanager: 8 alerts firing in cluster/eu-west-1: dcgm_down (sev=P2), node_exporter_restart_loop (sev=P3)
Jules: For short-term mitigation we can: 1) cordon + drain affected nodes and put them in a special pool, 2) fallback the pod to the image that bundles signed drivers, or 3) enable node-level `--allow-unsigned-modules` in kernel (not ideal).
Sam: Prefer option 1/2. We don't want to change kernel policies. Suggest patching the DaemonSet to add an initContainer that runs `modprobe --first-time nvidia || true` and retries with `modprobe nvidia_drm` — but that won't work if the module can't be signed.
Priya: Can we have the DaemonSet run a check and fallback to software metrics exporter (nvml stub) so DCGM doesn't crash the whole pod? Maybe a wrapper that exits with success and sets `dcgm_up=0` metric but doesn't restart.
Alex: Good idea — implement a small wrapper that exports a `/metrics` endpoint with `dcgm_up 0` until driver loads. That will silence flapping alerts and keep the SLO dashboards sane.
Sam: Also we should tune the Prometheus alert to add a 10m for `dcgm_up == 0` and require >2 nodes affected before firing — right now it goes off for single node flaps and causes pagers.
Jules: Agreed. I'll open PRs: 1) daemonset: add wrapper init logic + labeled rollout strategy, 2) prometheus: change rule threshold to `sum(dcgm_up == 0 by (node)) > 2 for 10m`.
Priya: Another ops item: ensure images we build for Dedicated customers include signed drivers for kernels we test against. This affects dedicated capacity billing if nodes go OOS. We lost ~700 GPU-minutes on scheduled workloads last night.
Alex: I'll follow up with build infra to add a signed driver variant and a test that boots a node and validates `nvidia-smi`.
infra-bot: [deploy] dcgm-exporter-wrapper v0.1 created (canary on gpu-pool-canary)
Sam: Can we also add a Grafana panel that shows driver-load success rate per kernel-version? That'll make the regressions obvious.
Jules: Will do — adding `gpu.driver_load_success{kernel_version}` and put it on the infra-health row of the GPU SLO dashboard.
Alex: Action summary: Sam/Jules implement wrapper + DaemonSet change; Jules adjust Prometheus rule; Alex coordinates signed-driver images with build; Priya tracks cost impact for the finance report. Ping here when canary is green. :thumbsup:
Priya: Canary looks ok so far, wrapper serving `dcgm_up 0` and no pager noise. Monitoring for 30m then rollout.
Sam: Noted — I'll also add a short doc in `eng-infra` about kernel-driver compatibility checks for future kernel bumps.
Jules: Thanks all — saved a noisy night.
Alex: Closing thread once rollout PR merged and build infra variant is live.
